What are Instagram Stories?

Instagram Stories are photos and videos that disappear 24 hours after posting. They launched in August 2016. When you watch someone's Story on Instagram itself, you show up in their viewer list. That's the reason this tool exists — viewing on AnonyIG keeps your name out of that list.

Why watch Stories anonymously?

Common reasons: checking what a competitor posted, browsing accounts you don't follow, watching public profiles without showing up in their viewer list. AnonyIG sits between you and Instagram — Instagram sees a request from our server, not from you.

Is AnonyIG free?

Yes. Stories, videos, highlights, reels — free to view and download. No paywall, no premium plan, no card required.

How to use AnonyIG

Find the account

Find the Instagram account you want to view. Copy the username (with or without @) or the full profile link.

Paste and search

Paste it into the search bar above and hit search. Stories load right away.

Watch or download

Watch them in your browser or save to your device. No login, no trail.

Yes, for public accounts in the United States. Instagram's own Terms of Use describe public profile content as visible to anyone on the open internet — viewing it through AnonyIG is the same act as visiting the profile in a browser, just without logging in. US courts have held that accessing publicly available web content does not violate the Computer Fraud and Abuse Act (CFAA); the landmark case is hiQ Labs v. LinkedIn (2022). AnonyIG never bypasses Instagram's authentication, never touches private accounts, and never stores the content past a short cache window. What you do with the downloaded media is on you: personal viewing is fine, redistributing someone else's copyrighted work isn't, regardless of how you got it.
Stories live 24 hours on Instagram. We cache the public ones, so you get roughly another 24-hour window after they leave the profile. Once Instagram's servers drop them, they're gone here too.

AnonyIG runs as a serverless proxy between you and Instagram's public content endpoints. When you paste a username, our backend resolves the profile against Instagram's public Graph, pulls the story manifest, and streams the media files back to your browser. The fetch happens server-side, which means Instagram only ever sees our IP — your IP, browser fingerprint, and any account state on your device never leave it. We don't keep search history or store cached files past a short rolling window (~24 hours), and there's no account layer to leak. The whole flow is plain HTTPS, no extension to install, no SDK. If a profile is set to private, the manifest comes back empty and the request stops there — we don't bypass Instagram's access controls.
We don't run premium tiers. DolphinRadar runs a freemium model, Inflact charges subscriptions. We don't, and there's no plan to start.
